fact: Binary search works on sorted search space and usually has O(log n) time complexity.
Breadth-first search usually uses a queue and explores level by level.
Depth-first search usually uses recursion or a stack.
Hash map lookup is average O(1), but worst case can be O(n).
Two pointers are often useful for sorted arrays, pair search, and window-like scans.
Sliding window is useful for contiguous subarray or substring problems.
